name: ADG1408YRUZ-REEL7
title: ADG1408/ADG1409: 4 Ω on resistance, 8-channel and differential 4-channel iCMOS multiplexers, ±15 V/+12 V/±5 V
summary: A pair of low on-resistance analog multiplexers built on the iCMOS high-voltage process. The ADG1408 routes one of eight inputs to one output under a 3-bit address; the ADG1409 routes one of four differential pairs to a differential output under a 2-bit address. An enable pin opens every switch. They run from ±4.5 V to ±16.5 V or a single 5 V to 16.5 V supply with rail-to-rail signals and 3 V-compatible logic. ADG1408YRUZ-REEL7 is the ADG1408 in 16-lead TSSOP.
key_figures: 4 Ω typ, 4.7 Ω max at 25°C, ±15 V
±4.5 V to ±16.5 V dual, 5 V to 16.5 V single

circuits.title: Figure 26. On resistance
circuits.description: A source VS sets the voltage on S; a current source draws IDS out of D, and a voltmeter across S and D reads the drop. RON is the drop divided by IDS.
notes: S stands for any source terminal, taken as S1, with its channel on.

circuits.title: Figure 27. Off leakage
circuits.description: With the switch off, VS drives S through an ammeter reading IS (Off) and VD drives D through an ammeter reading ID (Off).
notes: S stands for any source terminal, taken as S1.

circuits.title: Figure 28. On leakage
circuits.description: With the switch on and S left unconnected, VD drives D through an ammeter reading ID (On).
notes: S stands for any source terminal, taken as S1.

circuits.title: Figure 29. Address to output switching times, tTRANSITION
circuits.description: Measures the time from an address edge to the output settling on the newly chosen channel. A 0 V to 3 V pulse with edges under 20 ns drives all three address lines together, terminated by 50 Ω to ground. EN sits at 2.4 V. S1 and S8 carry two test voltages, S2 to S7 are grounded, and D drives 100 Ω parallel with 35 pF. tTRANSITION runs from the 50% point of the address edge to the 90% point of the output.

parts.value: pulse, 0 V to 3 V, tr and tf < 20 ns

notes: The ADG1409 is connected the same way.

circuits.title: Figure 30. Break-before-make delay, tBBM
circuits.description: Measures the gap during an address change when no channel is on. S1 and S8 are tied to the same test voltage, so the output only dips during the dead time. The address lines are driven together by a 0 V to 3 V pulse terminated in 50 Ω, EN is at 2.4 V, S2 to S7 are grounded and D drives 100 Ω parallel with 35 pF. tBBM is the time between the output falling through 80% and recovering through 80%.
notes: The ADG1409 is connected the same way.

circuits.title: Figure 31. Enable delay, tON (EN), tOFF (EN)
circuits.description: Measures how fast EN turns channel 1 on and off. All address lines are grounded so S1 is the chosen input; S1 carries the test voltage and S2 to S8 are grounded. A 0 V to 3 V pulse terminated in 50 Ω drives EN, and D drives 100 Ω parallel with 35 pF. Both delays run from the 50% point of the EN edge to the output reaching 90% of its swing (0.9 VO).
notes: The ADG1409 is connected the same way.

circuits.title: Figure 32. Charge injection
circuits.description: Measures the charge kicked onto the output when EN toggles. Address lines grounded select S1. A DC source VS behind RS feeds S1; D is loaded by CL = 1 nF to ground. A 0 V to 3 V square wave on EN switches the channel, and the step ΔVOUT on CL gives the injected charge.

parts.note: source resistance; 0 Ω in the charge-injection rows

notes: The ADG1409 is connected the same way. S is S1, the channel the grounded address selects.

circuits.title: Figure 33. Off isolation
circuits.description: A network analyser drives an off source terminal through its 50 Ω output and reads the drain through coax into RL = 50 Ω. The source terminal is also terminated in 50 Ω at the part. Each supply has 0.1 µF to ground. Off isolation = 20 log (VOUT / VS).
notes: S stands for any source terminal, taken as S1.

circuits.title: Figure 34. Channel-to-channel crosstalk
circuits.description: S2 is the on channel, driven by a network analyser through its source resistance, with D terminated in 50 Ω. S1, an off channel, goes through coax to the analyser input RL = 50 Ω. Each supply has 0.1 µF to ground. Crosstalk = 20 log (VOUT / VS).

circuits.title: Figure 35. Insertion loss
circuits.description: A network analyser drives the on channel's source terminal through its 50 Ω output and reads the drain through coax into RL = 50 Ω. Each supply has 0.1 µF to ground. Insertion loss = 20 log (VOUT with the switch / VOUT without it); the -3 dB bandwidth rows use the same setup.
notes: S stands for any source terminal, taken as S1.

circuits.title: Figure 36. THD + noise
circuits.description: An audio analyser drives the on channel's source terminal through RS with a sine of VS p-p and reads the drain, loaded by RL = 10 kΩ, through coax. A logic level VIN on the control input holds the switch on. Each supply has 0.1 µF to ground.
notes: S stands for any source terminal, taken as S1; IN is the enable input EN.

where.QINJ: charge moved onto the output when the switch turns
where.CL: load capacitance on D, 1 nF in the test

where.VOUT: signal at the drain with the switch off

equations.name: Insertion loss
equations.expr: Insertion loss = 20 log (VOUT with switch / VOUT without switch)

operation.text: The ADG1408 connects one of its eight sources S1 to S8 to the single drain D, picked by the 3-bit address A2 A1 A0. The ADG1409 connects one of four source pairs (SxA with SxB) to the drain pair DA, DB, picked by the 2-bit address A1 A0. EN high allows the addressed switch on; EN low opens every switch.

Dual supplies from ±4.5 V to ±16.5 V, or a single VDD of 5 V to 16.5 V with VSS at 0 V. VDD to VSS may not exceed 35 V. Specifications are given at ±15 V, +12 V and ±5 V. The analog signal may swing over the whole span from VSS to VDD.

A0 to A2 and EN read 2.0 V and above as high and 0.8 V and below as low at every supply, so 3 V logic drives them. Input current is ±0.1 µA max. Supply current rises while a logic input sits between the thresholds (Figure 16); with the inputs at 0 V or VDD, IDD and ISS are 1 µA max.
Changing the address opens the old channel before closing the new one (break-before-make, tBBM 30 ns min at ±15 V).
Signal may pass through any source or drain terminal in either direction.

The continuous current a channel can carry falls with temperature: for the ADG1408 at ±15 V it is 190 mA at 25°C, 105 mA at 85°C and 50 mA at 125°C. Pulses of 350 mA are allowed at 1 ms and 10% duty cycle.
Internal diodes to the supplies clamp the A, EN, S and D pins. A signal more than 0.3 V beyond VSS or VDD must have its current limited to 30 mA.
The LFCSP's exposed pad is joined to the die; it is soldered to VSS.
Figure 25 compares AC supply rejection with and without decoupling capacitors on the supplies; 0.1 µF capacitors on VDD and VSS are used in the AC test circuits.
